# This is idempotent - won't fail if table already exists with different schema
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -X -q -c "
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migrations (
  filename TEXT PRIMARY KEY,

);"

ALTER TABLE schema_migrations ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS checksum TEXT;" 2>/dev/null || true

# Handle legacy tables that have 'version' as PK instead of 'filename'
# Migrate any version-only rows to have filename
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -X -q -c "
DO \$\$
BEGIN
  -- Check if 'version' column exists
  IF EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns
    WHERE table_name = 'schema_migrations' AND column_name = 'version'
  ) THEN
    -- Add filename column if it doesn't exist
    IF NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns
      WHERE table_name = 'schema_migrations' AND column_name = 'filename'
    ) THEN
      ALTER TABLE schema_migrations ADD COLUMN filename TEXT;
    END IF;

    -- Update any rows where filename is NULL but version exists
    -- Try to find matching file by version prefix
    UPDATE schema_migrations SET filename = version || '.sql'
    WHERE filename IS NULL AND version IS NOT NULL;
  END IF;

applied_tmp="$(mktemp)"

# Query only the filename column (guaranteed to exist after our setup)
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -X -t -A -c "
SELECT filename FROM schema_migrations WHERE filename IS NOT NULL;" > "$applied_tmp" 2>/dev/null || true

for f in /app/database/migrations/*.sql; do

145	/**
146	 * Posture while the retention lane is open.
147	 *
148	 * 'refuse'  — do not delete when governed content exists; direct the member to
149	 *             a supported path. Currently in force.
150	 * 'proceed' — delete what this route can and report ONLY that, never implying
151	 *             completeness.
152	 *
153	 * The choice between these is a founder/legal decision, not an engineering one.
154	 * It is a single constant so it can be changed without touching logic.
155	 */
156	const CONTAINMENT_POSTURE: 'refuse' | 'proceed' = 'refuse';
157	
158	/**
159	 * Count governed content for a member, aggregated into member-legible
160	 * categories. Read-only — this function never mutates anything, which is the
161	 * property that makes a refused request safe to retry.
162	 */
163	async function governedContentFor(memberId: string): Promise<Array<{ label: string; rows: number }>> {
164	  const byLabel = new Map<string, number>();
165	  for (const { table, column, label } of GOVERNED_CONTENT) {
166	    try {
167	      const r = await query<{ n: string }>(
168	        `SELECT count(*)::text AS n FROM ${table} WHERE ${column} = $1`,
169	        [memberId],
170	      );
171	      const rows = Number(r.rows[0]?.n ?? 0);
172	      if (rows > 0) byLabel.set(label, (byLabel.get(label) ?? 0) + rows);
173	    } catch {
174	      // Table absent in this environment. Absence of a table is not evidence of
175	      // absence of content, so it is not counted — and because the posture is
176	      // refuse-by-default, an uncounted table cannot cause a wrongful deletion.
177	    }
178	  }
179	  return [...byLabel.entries()].map(([label, rows]) => ({ label, rows }));
180	}
181	
182	export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
183	  try {
184	    const body = await request.json().catch(() => ({} as Record<string, unknown>));
185	    const { memberId: claimedMemberId, confirmUsername } = body ?? {};
186	
187	    // 1. The actor comes from a verified session — never from the request body.
188	    //    getMemberIdFromRequest resolves an auth_sessions-backed credential and
189	    //    already rejects a mismatched x-member-id claim as impersonation.
190	    const memberId = await getMemberIdFromRequest(request);
191	    if (!memberId) {
192	      return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Authentication required' }, { status: 401 });
193	    }
194	
195	    // 2. A body-supplied id is not an input. If one is present and disagrees
196	    //    with the session, refuse — before any lookup or deletion runs.
197	    if (
198	      typeof claimedMemberId === 'string' &&
199	      claimedMemberId.length > 0 &&
200	      claimedMemberId !== memberId
201	    ) {
202	      return NextResponse.json(
203	        { error: 'You may only delete your own account' },
204	        { status: 403 },
205	      );
206	    }
207	
208	    // 3. Confirmation is compared against the SESSION-derived member's
209	    //    authoritative username. This is a destructive-action confirmation, not
210	    //    an authorization control — authorization was settled in step 1.
211	    const memberResult = await query<{ username: string }>(
212	      `SELECT username FROM members WHERE id = $1`,
213	      [memberId],
214	    );
215	
216	    if (memberResult.rows.length === 0) {
217	      return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Member not found' }, { status: 404 });
218	    }
219	
220	    if (confirmUsername !== memberResult.rows[0].username) {
221	      return NextResponse.json(
222	        { error: 'Username confirmation does not match' },
223	        { status: 400 },
224	      );
225	    }
226	
227	    // 3b. CONTAINMENT preflight — refuse rather than orphan.
228	    const governed = await governedContentFor(memberId);
229	    if (CONTAINMENT_POSTURE === 'refuse' && governed.length > 0) {
230	      return NextResponse.json(
231	        {
232	          error: 'deletion_incomplete_unavailable',
233	          // Plain language, and unambiguous about the one fact that matters
234	          // most to someone who just asked to be deleted: nothing happened.
235	          message:
236	            "We can't complete full account deletion automatically yet. Your account " +
237	            'and content have not been changed. Please contact support so we can ' +
238	            'handle your request safely.',
239	          accountChanged: false,
240	          nextStep: 'contact_support',
241	          retained: governed,
242	        },
243	        { status: 409 },
244	      );
245	    }
246	
247	    // 4. All-or-nothing. A partial failure must not leave an account that is
248	    //    half-deleted but still signed in.
249	    await transaction(async (tx) => {
250	      // Revoke credentials first: if anything below fails and rolls back, the
251	      // account is intact AND still usable. If it succeeds, no live session
252	      // outlives the member row.
253	      await tx.query(
254	        `UPDATE auth_sessions
255	            SET revoked = TRUE, revoked_at = NOW(), revoked_reason = 'account_deleted'
256	          WHERE member_id = $1 AND revoked = FALSE`,
257	        [memberId],
258	      );
259	
260	      await tx.query(`DELETE FROM member_settings WHERE member_id = $1`, [memberId]);
261	      await tx.query(`DELETE FROM member_sessions WHERE member_id = $1`, [memberId]);
262	
263	      // Best-effort tables, each in its own savepoint: a table missing in this
264	      // environment must not abort the whole transaction (the previous code
265	      // tolerated this with .catch(); inside a transaction a raw failure would
266	      // poison it).
267	      for (const { table, column } of OPTIONAL_CLEANUP) {
268	        await tx.query('SAVEPOINT optional_cleanup');
269	        try {
270	          await tx.query(`DELETE FROM ${table} WHERE ${column} = $1`, [memberId]);
271	          await tx.query('RELEASE SAVEPOINT optional_cleanup');
272	        } catch {
273	          await tx.query('ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT optional_cleanup');
274	        }
275	      }
276	
277	      // Studio doorway invitations are bound to the invited email's hash and are
278	      // not linked to the member, so the member cascade would leave them behind.
279	      // On erasure, remove this member's redemption and any invitation issued to
280	      // their email that no other member redeemed (2026-11-13 migration review
281	      // F2). Savepointed like the optional cleanup: environments without the
282	      // doorway tables must not abort the erasure.
283	      const emailRow = await tx.query<{ email: string | null }>(
284	        `SELECT email FROM members WHERE id = $1`, [memberId]);
285	      const email = emailRow.rows[0]?.email;
286	      await tx.query('SAVEPOINT doorway_cleanup');
287	      try {
288	        await tx.query(`DELETE FROM studio_doorway_redemptions WHERE member_id = $1`, [memberId]);
289	        if (email && email.trim()) {
290	          await tx.query(
291	            `DELETE FROM studio_doorway_invitations i
292	              WHERE i.email_sha256 = $1
293	                AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM studio_doorway_redemptions r WHERE r.invitation_id = i.id)`,
294	            [hashInvitedEmail(email)],
295	          );
296	        }
297	        await tx.query('RELEASE SAVEPOINT doorway_cleanup');
298	      } catch {
299	        await tx.query('ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT doorway_cleanup');
300	      }
301	
302	      await tx.query(`DELETE FROM members WHERE id = $1`, [memberId]);
303	    });
304	
305	    // Cookie removal is presentation cleanup; the credential was already
306	    // revoked inside the transaction above.
307	    await clearSessionCookie().catch(() => {});
308	
309	    // The response states ONLY what this route actually removed. It previously
310	    // claimed "Account and all associated data permanently deleted" while
311	    // journal, conversation, episodic and capsule content survived. A promise
312	    // about the disposition of someone's personal material must be one the
313	    // system can keep.
314	    return NextResponse.json({
315	      success: true,
316	      removed: ['account', 'settings', 'sessions', 'credentials'],
317	      message:
318	        'Your account has been closed and your sign-in credentials revoked.',
319	    });
320	  } catch (error) {
321	    console.error('[Delete Account API] Error:', error);
322	    return NextResponse.json(
323	      { error: 'Failed to delete account' },
324	      { status: 500 }
325	    );
326	  }
327	}

230	      return NextResponse.json(
231	        {
232	          error: 'deletion_incomplete_unavailable',
233	          // Plain language, and unambiguous about the one fact that matters
234	          // most to someone who just asked to be deleted: nothing happened.
235	          message:
236	            "We can't complete full account deletion automatically yet. Your account " +
237	            'and content have not been changed. Please contact support so we can ' +
238	            'handle your request safely.',
239	          accountChanged: false,
240	          nextStep: 'contact_support',
241	          retained: governed,
242	        },
243	        { status: 409 },
244	      );
245	    }
246	
247	    // 4. All-or-nothing. A partial failure must not leave an account that is
248	    //    half-deleted but still signed in.
249	    await transaction(async (tx) => {
250	      // Revoke credentials first: if anything below fails and rolls back, the
251	      // account is intact AND still usable. If it succeeds, no live session
252	      // outlives the member row.
253	      await tx.query(
254	        `UPDATE auth_sessions
255	            SET revoked = TRUE, revoked_at = NOW(), revoked_reason = 'account_deleted'
256	          WHERE member_id = $1 AND revoked = FALSE`,
257	        [memberId],
258	      );
259	
260	      await tx.query(`DELETE FROM member_settings WHERE member_id = $1`, [memberId]);
261	      await tx.query(`DELETE FROM member_sessions WHERE member_id = $1`, [memberId]);
262	
263	      // Best-effort tables, each in its own savepoint: a table missing in this
264	      // environment must not abort the whole transaction (the previous code
265	      // tolerated this with .catch(); inside a transaction a raw failure would
266	      // poison it).
267	      for (const { table, column } of OPTIONAL_CLEANUP) {
268	        await tx.query('SAVEPOINT optional_cleanup');
269	        try {
270	          await tx.query(`DELETE FROM ${table} WHERE ${column} = $1`, [memberId]);
271	          await tx.query('RELEASE SAVEPOINT optional_cleanup');
272	        } catch {
273	          await tx.query('ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT optional_cleanup');
274	        }
275	      }
276	
277	      // Studio doorway invitations are bound to the invited email's hash and are
278	      // not linked to the member, so the member cascade would leave them behind.
279	      // On erasure, remove this member's redemption and any invitation issued to
280	      // their email that no other member redeemed (2026-11-13 migration review
281	      // F2). Savepointed like the optional cleanup: environments without the
282	      // doorway tables must not abort the erasure.
283	      const emailRow = await tx.query<{ email: string | null }>(
284	        `SELECT email FROM members WHERE id = $1`, [memberId]);
285	      const email = emailRow.rows[0]?.email;
286	      await tx.query('SAVEPOINT doorway_cleanup');
287	      try {
288	        await tx.query(`DELETE FROM studio_doorway_redemptions WHERE member_id = $1`, [memberId]);
289	        if (email && email.trim()) {
290	          await tx.query(
291	            `DELETE FROM studio_doorway_invitations i
292	              WHERE i.email_sha256 = $1
293	                AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM studio_doorway_redemptions r WHERE r.invitation_id = i.id)`,
294	            [hashInvitedEmail(email)],
295	          );
296	        }
297	        await tx.query('RELEASE SAVEPOINT doorway_cleanup');
298	      } catch {
299	        await tx.query('ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT doorway_cleanup');
300	      }
301	
302	      await tx.query(`DELETE FROM members WHERE id = $1`, [memberId]);
303	    });
304	
305	    // Cookie removal is presentation cleanup; the credential was already
306	    // revoked inside the transaction above.
307	    await clearSessionCookie().catch(() => {});
308	
309	    // The response states ONLY what this route actually removed. It previously
310	    // claimed "Account and all associated data permanently deleted" while
311	    // journal, conversation, episodic and capsule content survived. A promise
312	    // about the disposition of someone's personal material must be one the
313	    // system can keep.
314	    return NextResponse.json({
315	      success: true,
316	      removed: ['account', 'settings', 'sessions', 'credentials'],
317	      message:
318	        'Your account has been closed and your sign-in credentials revoked.',
319	    });
320	  } catch (error) {
321	    console.error('[Delete Account API] Error:', error);
322	    return NextResponse.json(
323	      { error: 'Failed to delete account' },
324	      { status: 500 }
325	    );
326	  }
327	}

112	# DEPLOYMENT-SAFETY-01 (founder ruling 2026-09-14). The migration runner already
113	# exits non-zero on the first failing file; both deploy paths used to catch that
114	# with `if ! …; then log_warn …; fi` and carry on to "Deployment complete!".
115	#
116	# That swallow broke the migrations README's own rule — *schema and reader ship
117	# together* — IN THE FAILURE DIRECTION: the schema could fail while the reader
118	# continued toward production, and the operator was told the deploy succeeded.
119	# A green deploy was not evidence that any migration ran.

121	#   migration success  →  deployment may continue
122	#   migration failure  →  deployment STOPS, non-zero, no success message
123	#
124	# DEPLOYMENT-SAFETY-03 / STEP 3 strengthens the ordering after the original
125	# fail-closed repair: an exact admitted review must establish final-schema and
126	# every-prefix old-reader compatibility before pending migrations may run.

129	#   build → image provenance → review/compatibility gate
130	#         → re-witness pending set + old reader → migrate
131	#         → rollback tags → candidate swap → running provenance

133	# A migration failure therefore leaves the candidate reader unswapped. Because
134	# the runner commits each migration independently, the admitted review must also
135	# cover every successfully committed prefix that could remain after failure.

142	# engine. Bootstrap/test/reconstruction databases are not production authority.

419	# ALERT - Send alert to developer via /api/build/alert
420	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
421	send_alert() {
422	    local severity="$1"
423	    local message="$2"
424	    local details="${3:-}"
425	
426	    # Get BASE_URL from env file (quote-safe, whitespace-trimmed), allow env override
427	    local base_url
428	    base_url=$(awk -F= '/^BASE_URL=/{gsub(/^"|"$/,"",$2); gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/,"",$2); print $2}' .env.production 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)
429	    base_url="${BASE_URL:-${base_url:-https://soullab.life}}"
430	    base_url="${base_url%/}"  # Strip trailing slash
431	
432	    # Get alert token from env file (quote-safe, whitespace-trimmed), allow env override
433	    local alert_token
434	    alert_token=$(awk -F= '/^INTERNAL_ALERT_TOKEN=/{gsub(/^"|"$/,"",$2); gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/,"",$2); print $2}' .env.production 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)
435	    alert_token="${INTERNAL_ALERT_TOKEN:-$alert_token}"
436	
437	    # Build JSON payload safely using jq if available
438	    local json_payload
439	    if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
440	        if [ -n "$details" ]; then
441	            # Validate details is valid JSON, otherwise treat as string
442	            if echo "$details" | jq -e . >/dev/null 2>&1; then
443	                json_payload=$(jq -n \
444	                    --arg sev "$severity" \
445	                    --arg msg "$message" \
446	                    --arg commit "${GIT_COMMIT:-unknown}" \
447	                    --argjson details "$details" \
448	                    '{severity:$sev, message:$msg, commit:$commit, source:"deploy-script", details:$details}')
449	            else
450	                json_payload=$(jq -n \
451	                    --arg sev "$severity" \
452	                    --arg msg "$message" \
453	                    --arg commit "${GIT_COMMIT:-unknown}" \
454	                    --arg details "$details" \
455	                    '{severity:$sev, message:$msg, commit:$commit, source:"deploy-script", details:$details}')
456	            fi
457	        else
458	            json_payload=$(jq -n \
459	                --arg sev "$severity" \
460	                --arg msg "$message" \
461	                --arg commit "${GIT_COMMIT:-unknown}" \
462	                '{severity:$sev, message:$msg, commit:$commit, source:"deploy-script"}')
463	        fi
464	    else
465	        # Fallback: escape quotes in message
466	        local escaped_msg
467	        escaped_msg=$(echo "$message" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g')
468	        if [ -n "$details" ]; then
469	            json_payload="{\"severity\": \"$severity\", \"message\": \"$escaped_msg\", \"commit\": \"${GIT_COMMIT:-unknown}\", \"source\": \"deploy-script\", \"details\": $details}"
470	        else
471	            json_payload="{\"severity\": \"$severity\", \"message\": \"$escaped_msg\", \"commit\": \"${GIT_COMMIT:-unknown}\", \"source\": \"deploy-script\"}"
472	        fi
473	    fi
474	
475	    # Report WHY a send fails: a silent alert path is how an incident goes unnoticed.
476	    #   503 server_not_configured  → INTERNAL_ALERT_TOKEN unset in the app container
477	    #   503 alert_smtp_not_configured / alert_sender_mismatch → ALERT_SMTP_* / ALERT_FROM
478	    #   401 → token here differs from the container's
479	    local alert_http alert_body
480	    alert_body=$(mktemp)
481	    alert_http=$(curl -s -o "$alert_body" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "${base_url}/api/build/alert" \
482	        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
483	        -H "x-internal-token: ${alert_token}" \
484	        -d "$json_payload" 2>/dev/null) || alert_http="000"
485	    if [ "${alert_http:0:1}" != "2" ]; then
486	        local alert_err
487	        alert_err=$(grep -o '"error":"[a-z_]*"' "$alert_body" 2>/dev/null | head -n1)
488	        [ -z "$alert_token" ] && alert_err="${alert_err:+$alert_err; }no INTERNAL_ALERT_TOKEN on the deploy host"
489	        log_warn "Alert send FAILED (non-critical): HTTP ${alert_http}${alert_err:+ — $alert_err}"
490	    fi
491	    rm -f "$alert_body"
492	}

762	# DEPLOY - Build and start the stack
763	# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
764	cmd_deploy() {
765	    local ref="${1:-}"
766	    # The lock record names the ASSERTED target (the SHA on the command line),
767	    # never the shared checkout's HEAD — see scripts/deploy-lock.sh.
768	    acquire_deploy_lock "deploy-production.sh deploy" "$ref"
769	    log_info "Deploying MAIA Sovereign..."
770	
771	    cd "$PROJECT_DIR"
772	
773	    # Name a commit and snapshot it into an isolated build context BEFORE any
774	    # build work. Refuses when no SHA is named (unless DEPLOY_ALLOW_HEAD=1). This
775	    # is the structural guarantee that the full deploy builds an explicitly named
776	    # immutable commit, never whichever branch happens to be checked out in the
777	    # shared repo. Sets MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT + GIT_COMMIT.
778	    deploy_ctx_assert_and_materialize "$ref" || exit 1
779	    deploy_ctx_assert_descends_from_running "deploy-production.sh deploy" || exit 1
780	
781	    # Verify .env.production exists
782	    if [ ! -f ".env.production" ]; then
783	        log_error ".env.production not found. Run: ./scripts/deploy-production.sh setup"
784	        exit 1
785	    fi
786	
787	    # Check required values are set
788	    if grep -q "REPLACE_ME" .env.production; then
789	        log_error "Please replace all REPLACE_ME values in .env.production"
790	        exit 1
791	    fi
792	
793	    # Dependency security audit — target-declared manager, fail closed at moderate+.
794	    run_dependency_security_audit || exit 1
795	
796	    # Build and start
797	    log_info "Building Docker images..."
798	    # GIT_COMMIT was exported from the asserted SHA by materialize above — do NOT
799	    # re-resolve it from HEAD here (that would re-couple us to the shared checkout).
800	    # APP_VERSION is read from the SNAPSHOT so it matches the deployed commit.
801	    export APP_VERSION="$(node -p "require('$MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT/package.json').version" 2>/dev/null || echo '1.0.0')"
802	    export BUILD_DATE="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
803	    log_info "Deploying commit: $GIT_COMMIT (v$APP_VERSION)"
804	
805	    # Disk preflight — refuse BEFORE the storage-expanding build (a full-disk
806	    # build dies at metadata write after minutes and can exit 0 through ssh).
807	    "$SCRIPT_DIR/pre-deploy-gate.sh" disk
808	
809	    # Build image first (never rebuild while down!) — from the immutable snapshot
810	    # (compose reads MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT for every build `context:`).
811	    # Build + swap use the SNAPSHOT's compose file (deploy_ctx_compose) — the
812	    # deployment structure is the authorized commit's (2026-09-03 provenance repair).
813	    # :prod guard: the build moves :prod; restore it if we stop before the swap.
814	    prod_tag_guard_arm "$GIT_COMMIT"
815	    deploy_ctx_compose build \
816	        --build-arg GIT_COMMIT="$GIT_COMMIT" \
817	        --build-arg APP_VERSION="$APP_VERSION" \
818	        --build-arg BUILD_DATE="$BUILD_DATE"
819	
820	    # PRE-swap: the built image must carry the asserted stamp; abort before any swap.
821	    deploy_ctx_verify_image "$GIT_COMMIT" "$MAIA_IMAGE_REPO:prod" || exit 1
822	
823	    # REVIEW-CUSTODY + DS-03: the exact pending relation must carry an
824	    # admitted review, exact old-reader compatibility, and failure-prefix safety.
825	    review_migration_custody_or_abort "Deployment"
826	
827	    # STEP 3: migrate while the reviewed old reader is still live. The helper
828	    # re-derives the pending set and re-witnesses the old reader immediately
829	    # before invoking the runner. Failure exits here, before tags or candidate swap.
830	    run_migrations_or_abort "Deployment"
831	
832	    # Only a successful pre-swap migration may advance rollback roles or the reader.
833	    # From here the candidate is the legitimate :prod.
834	    prod_tag_guard_disarm
835	    tag_images_for_rollback "$GIT_COMMIT"
836	
837	    log_info "Starting containers after successful migrations..."
838	    deploy_ctx_compose up -d
839	
840	    log_info "Waiting for services to be healthy..."
841	    sleep 10
842	
843	    # Post-swap: assert the running container is the commit we authorized.
844	    if ! deploy_ctx_verify_running "$GIT_COMMIT"; then
845	        log_error "Post-swap provenance verification FAILED — the running container does not report the"
846	        log_error "authorized immutable commit $GIT_COMMIT. Migrations already succeeded pre-swap."
847	        log_error "The reviewed old reader was compatible with the resulting schema; restore the"
848	        log_error "previous reader image if the candidate cannot be made live (rollback stops the"
849	        log_error "candidate and refuses to swap if scripts/rollback-guards/ finds rows the old reader"
850	        log_error "cannot read; it prints the repair to run first):"
851	        log_error "  ./scripts/deploy-production.sh rollback"
852	        exit 1

#!/bin/bash
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# MAIA Sovereign - Production Deployment Script
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Usage:
#   ./scripts/deploy-production.sh [command]
#
# Commands:
#   setup     - First-time setup (generate secrets, prepare env)
#   deploy    - Build and deploy the full stack
#   update    - Pull latest code and redeploy
#   rollback  - Rollback to previous deployment (2-command rollback)
#   safe-mode - Toggle safe mode (on/off) for degraded operation
#   migrate   - Run database migrations
#   logs      - Tail container logs
#   status    - Show container status
#   stop      - Stop all containers
#   backup    - Backup database to file
#   restore   - Restore database from backup
#
# Stability Features:
#   - Image tagging by git SHA for instant rollbacks
#   - Safe mode toggle for degraded operation
#   - Smoke tests with automatic alerts
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
PROJECT_DIR="$(dirname "$SCRIPT_DIR")"
COMPOSE_FILE="$PROJECT_DIR/docker-compose.production.yml"

# Deploy lane lock — every mutating command serializes on $PROJECT_DIR/.deploy.lock
# so concurrent deploys are structurally impossible (see scripts/deploy-lock.sh).
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/deploy-lock.sh"

# Rollback tagging — shared with pre-deploy-gate.sh so EVERY deploy path keeps
# maia-sovereign:current/:previous/:<sha> truthful (see scripts/deploy-tag.sh).
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/deploy-tag.sh"

# Immutable-SHA build context — deploy/update build a NAMED commit materialized
# into an isolated context, never whatever branch is checked out in the shared
# repo (2026-07-27 incident). See scripts/deploy-context.sh + docs/ops/IMMUTABLE_SHA_DEPLOY.md.
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/deploy-context.sh"

# Colors for output
RED='\033[0;31m'
GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
BLUE='\033[0;34m'
NC='\033[0m' # No Color

log_info() { echo -e "${BLUE}[INFO]${NC} $1"; }
log_success() { echo -e "${GREEN}[OK]${NC} $1"; }
log_warn() { echo -e "${YELLOW}[WARN]${NC} $1"; }
log_error() { echo -e "${RED}[ERROR]${NC} $1"; }


run_dependency_security_audit() {
    # Audit the TARGET, never the shared checkout: the audit must read the same
    # lockfile the image is built from (2026-10-31 — it ran from $PROJECT_DIR and
    # audited a stale checkout's lockfile instead of the immutable snapshot).
    local audit_dir="${MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT:-$PROJECT_DIR}"
    local manifest="$audit_dir/package.json"
    local declared manager fix_hint
    local -a audit_cmd

    declared="$(node -p "require('$manifest').packageManager || ''" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    manager="${declared%%@*}"
    if [ -z "$manager" ]; then
        if [ -f "${MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT:-$PROJECT_DIR}/package-lock.json" ]; then
            manager="npm"
        elif [ -f "${MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT:-$PROJECT_DIR}/pnpm-lock.yaml" ]; then
            manager="pnpm"
        fi
    fi

    log_info "Running dependency security audit${declared:+ (declared $declared)}..."

    case "$manager" in
        npm)
            command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1 || { log_error "Declared package manager npm is unavailable — dependency audit cannot run."; return 1; }
            # Fails closed at moderate+; honours only live, dated entries in the
            # snapshot's security/npm-audit-exceptions.json.
            audit_cmd=(node "$audit_dir/scripts/deploy-audit-gate.mjs" "$audit_dir")
            fix_hint="npm audit fix"
            ;;
        pnpm)
            command -v pnpm >/dev/null 2>&1 || { log_error "Declared package manager pnpm is unavailable — dependency audit cannot run."; return 1; }
            audit_cmd=(pnpm audit --prod --audit-level=moderate)
            fix_hint="pnpm audit --fix"
            ;;
        *)
            log_error "No supported package manager could be resolved from the target snapshot."
            return 1
            ;;
    esac

    if ! (cd "$audit_dir" && "${audit_cmd[@]}") 2>&1; then
        log_error "Dependency audit failed — moderate+ production vulnerabilities detected."
        log_error "Review and remediate deliberately; do not apply fixes blindly."
        log_error "Package-manager hint: $fix_hint"
        return 1
    fi

    log_success "Dependency audit passed"
}

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# MIGRATIONS - fail closed
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# DEPLOYMENT-SAFETY-01 (founder ruling 2026-09-14). The migration runner already
# exits non-zero on the first failing file; both deploy paths used to catch that
# with `if ! …; then log_warn …; fi` and carry on to "Deployment complete!".
#
# That swallow broke the migrations README's own rule — *schema and reader ship
# together* — IN THE FAILURE DIRECTION: the schema could fail while the reader
# continued toward production, and the operator was told the deploy succeeded.
# A green deploy was not evidence that any migration ran.
#
#   migration success  →  deployment may continue
#   migration failure  →  deployment STOPS, non-zero, no success message
#
# DEPLOYMENT-SAFETY-03 / STEP 3 strengthens the ordering after the original
# fail-closed repair: an exact admitted review must establish final-schema and
# every-prefix old-reader compatibility before pending migrations may run.
#
# Normal deploy/update now order:
#   build → image provenance → review/compatibility gate
#         → re-witness pending set + old reader → migrate
#         → rollback tags → candidate swap → running provenance
#
# A migration failure therefore leaves the candidate reader unswapped. Because
# the runner commits each migration independently, the admitted review must also
# cover every successfully committed prefix that could remain after failure.
#
# ⛔ NOT CHANGED: migration discovery, selection, per-file transaction semantics,
# the ledger, migration contents, or the migration-only command's role.
# REVIEW-CUSTODY-01 / STEP 3 — production migration review preflight.
#
# This belongs at the DEPLOYMENT surface, not in the generic local migration
# engine. Bootstrap/test/reconstruction databases are not production authority.
# The pending set is derived read-only from the exact migration context + ledger,
# and every pending SQL file must carry a physically witnessed Read event.
_review_migration_compose() {
    if [ -n "${MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT:-}" ]; then
        deploy_ctx_compose "$@"
    else
        docker compose -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" "$@"
    fi
}

collect_pending_production_migrations() {
    local raw
    if ! raw="$(_review_migration_compose --profile migrate run --rm -T migrate sh -c '
        set -eu
        ledger="$(mktemp)"
        trap '"'"'rm -f "$ledger"'"'"' EXIT
        psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "SELECT filename FROM schema_migrations WHERE filename IS NOT NULL ORDER BY 1" > "$ledger"
        for f in /app/database/migrations/*.sql; do
            [ -e "$f" ] || continue
            b="${f##*/}"
            if ! grep -Fxq "$b" "$ledger"; then
                printf "database/migrations/%s\n" "$b"
            fi
        done
    ')"; then
        log_error "⛔ Could not derive the production-pending migration set read-only."
        log_error "   REVIEW-CUSTODY refuses rather than guessing what would execute."
        return 1
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$raw" | grep -E '^database/migrations/[^/]+\.sql$' || true
}

# FOUNDER-BETA-MIGRATION-01: one-time exact-byte exception (not a security verdict).
# Preserve pending-set recheck, migration fail-stop, old reader, rollback and image stamps.
founder_college_essay_beta_migration_or_abort() {
    local target="$1" pending="$2" context="$3"
    local expected_path="database/migrations/20261113000010_studio_doorway_invitation_studio_access.sql"
    local expected_hash="1bb1aabd9ee36a34a8028abe658efc4608c6c5088cebe82a090a30022acc9062"
    local base="352a6e410ac6212601ec642a58c940bdcca9965b"
    local old="faac1d4824cff4504ea814678e5e8270abc60fa6"
    local old_image="sha256:a9317ce76e58a34bfa83d80dbc68d4d66020959dafa64bd4c95ba06d017fad97"
    local rollback_image="sha256:ba28b98a3adc73a4962efac222ffcf8e7d87c7b961ea8da35940387dac9e61db"
    local name hash live_stamp live_sha state

    if [ "$pending" != "$expected_path" ] ||
       ! git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" merge-base --is-ancestor "$base" "$target"; then
        log_error "FOUNDER-BETA: unexpected pending set or source ancestry."
        return 1
    fi
    # No application, invitation-auth, or data-model changes after the frozen candidate.
    while IFS= read -r name; do
        case "$name" in
            scripts/deploy-production.sh|scripts/verify-college-essay-beta-migration-exception.sh) ;;
            *) log_error "FOUNDER-BETA: changed source not covered: $name"; return 1 ;;
        esac
    done < <(git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" diff --name-only "$base" "$target")
    if [ ! -f "$context/$expected_path" ]; then
        log_error "FOUNDER-BETA: immutable migration missing."
        return 1
    fi
    if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        hash="$(sha256sum "$context/$expected_path" | awk '{print $1}')"
    elif command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        hash="$(shasum -a 256 "$context/$expected_path" | awk '{print $1}')"
    else
        log_error "FOUNDER-BETA: no SHA-256 tool."; return 1
    fi
    if [ "$hash" != "$expected_hash" ]; then
        log_error "FOUNDER-BETA: migration byte hash mismatch."; return 1
    fi
    live_stamp="$(docker exec maia-sovereign printenv GIT_COMMIT 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
    live_sha="$(git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" rev-parse "$live_stamp^{commit}" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
    if [ "$live_sha" != "$old" ] ||
       [ "$(docker inspect maia-sovereign -f '{{.Image}}' 2>/dev/null)" != "$old_image" ] ||
       [ "$(docker image inspect maia-sovereign:previous -f '{{.Id}}' 2>/dev/null)" != "$rollback_image" ]; then
        log_error "FOUNDER-BETA: old reader, running image, or rollback image changed."
        return 1
    fi
    state="$(docker exec maia-postgres psql -U soullab -d maia_consciousness -Atqc \
        "SELECT CASE WHEN to_regclass('public.studio_doorway_invitations') IS NOT NULL \
         AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema='public' AND table_name='studio_doorway_invitations' AND column_name='issuer_member_id') \
         AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema='public' AND table_name='studio_doorway_invitations' AND column_name='grants_writers_studio') \
         THEN 'ready' ELSE 'refuse' END" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
    if [ "$state" != "ready" ]; then
        log_error "FOUNDER-BETA: schema is not the expected pre-migration shape."
        return 1
    fi
    MIGRATION_COMPAT_EXPECTED_OLD_READER="$live_sha"
    log_warn "FOUNDER-BETA: exact single-migration documentary-review exception admitted."
    log_warn "FOUNDER-BETA: not independently security-reviewed. All mutation/rollback gates remain."
    return 0
}

review_migration_custody_or_abort() {
    local phase="$1"

    # Cache only observations that have actually passed the composed gate.
    # Step 3 will re-witness them immediately before schema mutation.
    MIGRATION_COMPAT_EXPECTED_PENDING=""
    MIGRATION_COMPAT_EXPECTED_OLD_READER=""

    local target="${DEPLOY_CTX_FULL_SHA:-}"
    if [ -z "$target" ]; then
        target="$(git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
    fi
    if [ -z "$target" ]; then
        log_error "⛔ REVIEW-CUSTODY cannot resolve the exact migration target commit."
        return 1
    fi

    local pending
    if ! pending="$(collect_pending_production_migrations)"; then
        log_error "$phase aborted before migration: pending-set witness failed."
        return 1
    fi
    MIGRATION_COMPAT_EXPECTED_PENDING="$pending"
    if [ -z "$pending" ]; then
        log_info "REVIEW-CUSTODY: no production-pending migrations; no migration review required."
        return 0
    fi

    # Founder-authorized opt-in exception for ONE additive College Essay beta migration.
    if [ -n "${SOULLAB_BETA_MIGRATION_POLICY:-}" ]; then
        if [ "$SOULLAB_BETA_MIGRATION_POLICY" != "college-essay-20261113-single-additive" ]; then
            log_error "FOUNDER-BETA: unknown migration exception; refusing."
            return 1
        fi
        if ! founder_college_essay_beta_migration_or_abort "$target" "$pending" "${MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT:-$PROJECT_DIR}"; then
            log_error "FOUNDER-BETA: preflight refused; no schema mutation."
            return 1
        fi
        return 0
    fi

    local record="${REVIEW_CUSTODY_RECORD:-}"
    local review="${REVIEW_CUSTODY_REVIEW:-}"
    local trace="${REVIEW_CUSTODY_TRACE:-}"
    if [ -z "$record" ] || [ -z "$review" ] || [ -z "$trace" ]; then
        log_error "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
        log_error "⛔ DATABASE MIGRATION REVIEW REQUIRED — $phase REFUSED"
        log_error "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
        log_error "Pending migrations exist, but the bound evidence triplet is incomplete."
        log_error "Set REVIEW_CUSTODY_RECORD, REVIEW_CUSTODY_REVIEW, REVIEW_CUSTODY_TRACE."
        log_error "Self-reported coverage is not accepted."
        printf '%s\n' "$pending" | sed 's/^/  pending: /' >&2
        return 1
    fi

    local gate_root="${MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT:-$PROJECT_DIR}"
    local gate="$gate_root/scripts/review-custody-migration-gate.ts"
    if [ ! -f "$gate" ]; then
        log_error "⛔ Migration review gate is absent from target context: $gate"
        return 1
    fi
    local tsx_bin="$PROJECT_DIR/node_modules/.bin/tsx"
    if [ ! -x "$tsx_bin" ]; then
        log_error "⛔ Migration review gate cannot execute: host tsx unavailable at $tsx_bin"
        return 1
    fi

    # DEPLOYMENT-SAFETY-03 / STEP 2B: compatibility is relational to
    # the reader that is actually live before any swap. Missing/unresolvable
    # identity refuses; a guessed old reader would make compatibility meaningless.
    local old_stamp old_reader
    old_stamp="$(docker exec maia-sovereign printenv GIT_COMMIT 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ -z "$old_stamp" ]; then
        log_error "⛔ MIGRATION-COMPATIBILITY cannot identify the currently running reader."
        return 1
    fi
    old_reader="$(git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" rev-parse "$old_stamp^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ -z "$old_reader" ]; then
        log_error "⛔ Running reader stamp does not resolve to a repository commit: $old_stamp"
        return 1
    fi

    local args=(--record "$record" --review "$review" --trace "$trace"
                --repo "$PROJECT_DIR" --target "$target" --old-reader "$old_reader")
    local m
    while IFS= read -r m; do
        [ -n "$m" ] && args+=(--migration "$m")
    done <<< "$pending"

    log_info "REVIEW-CUSTODY + MIGRATION-COMPATIBILITY: checking exact pending relation..."
    if ! "$tsx_bin" "$gate" "${args[@]}"; then
        log_error "⛔ $phase aborted before migration: review/compatibility gate does not apply."
        return 1
    fi
    MIGRATION_COMPAT_EXPECTED_OLD_READER="$old_reader"
    log_success "Migration review custody + old-reader compatibility apply to the exact pending set"
}

rewitness_migration_relation_or_abort() {
    local phase="$1"
    local expected_pending="${MIGRATION_COMPAT_EXPECTED_PENDING-}"
    local expected_old="${MIGRATION_COMPAT_EXPECTED_OLD_READER-}"

    # Re-derive the mutable ledger relation immediately before mutation. The
    # target tree is immutable; the production ledger and live reader are not.
    local pending_now
    if ! pending_now="$(collect_pending_production_migrations)"; then
        log_error "⛔ $phase aborted before migration: could not re-witness the pending set."
        return 1
    fi
    if [ "$pending_now" != "$expected_pending" ]; then
        log_error "⛔ $phase aborted before migration: pending migration state moved after review."
        log_error "   The compatibility claim applies only to the exact ordered set it reviewed."
        return 1
    fi

    # If there is schema work to do, the old reader is the load-bearing recovery
    # relation. Read it LAST, immediately before the migration runner.
    if [ -n "$expected_pending" ]; then
        if [ -z "$expected_old" ]; then
            log_error "⛔ $phase aborted before migration: no reviewed old-reader identity is cached."
            return 1
        fi

        local live_stamp live_old
        live_stamp="$(docker exec maia-sovereign printenv GIT_COMMIT 2>/dev/null || true)"
        if [ -z "$live_stamp" ]; then
            log_error "⛔ $phase aborted before migration: the live reader identity cannot be read."
            return 1
        fi
        live_old="$(git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" rev-parse "$live_stamp^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
        if [ -z "$live_old" ] || [ "$live_old" != "$expected_old" ]; then
            log_error "⛔ $phase aborted before migration: the live reader moved after compatibility review."
            log_error "   reviewed: $expected_old"
            log_error "   live:     ${live_old:-unresolved}"
            return 1
        fi
        log_success "Old reader re-witnessed immediately before migration: $live_old"
    fi
}

run_migrations_or_abort() {
    local phase="$1"

    # STEP 3 ordering law: no schema mutation occurs unless the mutable parts of
    # the reviewed relation still match at the last possible pre-migration point.
    if ! rewitness_migration_relation_or_abort "$phase"; then
        exit 1
    fi

    log_info "Running database migrations before candidate swap..."
    if deploy_ctx_compose --profile migrate run --rm migrate; then
        log_success "Migrations applied before candidate swap"
        return 0
    fi

    echo ""
    log_error "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
    log_error "⛔ DATABASE MIGRATIONS FAILED — DEPLOYMENT ABORTED PRE-SWAP"
    log_error "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
    log_error ""
    log_error "The candidate reader was NOT swapped in."
    log_error "The previously witnessed old reader remains the live reader."
    log_error "Any earlier migration in this run that committed successfully was"
    log_error "required by the admitted review to leave that old reader compatible"
    log_error "at every committed prefix."
    log_error ""
    log_error "The runner stops at the first failing file. Later migrations are"
    log_error "unapplied and this deployment is NOT complete."
    log_error ""
    log_error "Inspect what committed and what remains before any retry:"
    log_error "  docker exec maia-postgres psql -U soullab -d maia_consciousness \\"
    log_error "    -c \"SELECT filename FROM schema_migrations ORDER BY applied_at DESC LIMIT 10;\""
    log_error ""
    log_error "Do not swap the candidate reader until a newly applicable review/"
    log_error "compatibility record governs the remaining exact pending set."
    log_error "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
    echo ""
    log_error "$phase aborted pre-swap: migrations did not succeed."
    exit 1
}

# ALERT - Send alert to developer via /api/build/alert
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
send_alert() {
    local severity="$1"
    local message="$2"
    local details="${3:-}"

    # Get BASE_URL from env file (quote-safe, whitespace-trimmed), allow env override
    local base_url
    base_url=$(awk -F= '/^BASE_URL=/{gsub(/^"|"$/,"",$2); gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/,"",$2); print $2}' .env.production 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)
    base_url="${BASE_URL:-${base_url:-https://soullab.life}}"
    base_url="${base_url%/}"  # Strip trailing slash

    # Get alert token from env file (quote-safe, whitespace-trimmed), allow env override
    local alert_token
    alert_token=$(awk -F= '/^INTERNAL_ALERT_TOKEN=/{gsub(/^"|"$/,"",$2); gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/,"",$2); print $2}' .env.production 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)
    alert_token="${INTERNAL_ALERT_TOKEN:-$alert_token}"

    # Build JSON payload safely using jq if available
    local json_payload
    if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        if [ -n "$details" ]; then
            # Validate details is valid JSON, otherwise treat as string
            if echo "$details" | jq -e . >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                json_payload=$(jq -n \
                    --arg sev "$severity" \
                    --arg msg "$message" \
                    --arg commit "${GIT_COMMIT:-unknown}" \
                    --argjson details "$details" \
                    '{severity:$sev, message:$msg, commit:$commit, source:"deploy-script", details:$details}')
            else
                json_payload=$(jq -n \
                    --arg sev "$severity" \
                    --arg msg "$message" \
                    --arg commit "${GIT_COMMIT:-unknown}" \
                    --arg details "$details" \
                    '{severity:$sev, message:$msg, commit:$commit, source:"deploy-script", details:$details}')
            fi
        else
            json_payload=$(jq -n \
                --arg sev "$severity" \
                --arg msg "$message" \
                --arg commit "${GIT_COMMIT:-unknown}" \
                '{severity:$sev, message:$msg, commit:$commit, source:"deploy-script"}')
        fi
    else
        # Fallback: escape quotes in message
        local escaped_msg
        escaped_msg=$(echo "$message" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g')
        if [ -n "$details" ]; then
            json_payload="{\"severity\": \"$severity\", \"message\": \"$escaped_msg\", \"commit\": \"${GIT_COMMIT:-unknown}\", \"source\": \"deploy-script\", \"details\": $details}"
        else
            json_payload="{\"severity\": \"$severity\", \"message\": \"$escaped_msg\", \"commit\": \"${GIT_COMMIT:-unknown}\", \"source\": \"deploy-script\"}"
        fi
    fi

    # Report WHY a send fails: a silent alert path is how an incident goes unnoticed.
    #   503 server_not_configured  → INTERNAL_ALERT_TOKEN unset in the app container
    #   503 alert_smtp_not_configured / alert_sender_mismatch → ALERT_SMTP_* / ALERT_FROM
    #   401 → token here differs from the container's
    local alert_http alert_body
    alert_body=$(mktemp)
    alert_http=$(curl -s -o "$alert_body" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "${base_url}/api/build/alert" \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -H "x-internal-token: ${alert_token}" \
        -d "$json_payload" 2>/dev/null) || alert_http="000"
    if [ "${alert_http:0:1}" != "2" ]; then
        local alert_err
        alert_err=$(grep -o '"error":"[a-z_]*"' "$alert_body" 2>/dev/null | head -n1)
        [ -z "$alert_token" ] && alert_err="${alert_err:+$alert_err; }no INTERNAL_ALERT_TOKEN on the deploy host"
        log_warn "Alert send FAILED (non-critical): HTTP ${alert_http}${alert_err:+ — $alert_err}"
    fi
    rm -f "$alert_body"
}

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SMOKE TESTS - Run post-deployment health checks
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
run_smoke_tests() {
    log_info "Running post-deployment smoke tests..."

    # Quote-safe, whitespace-trimmed BASE_URL parsing, allow env override
    local base_url
    base_url=$(awk -F= '/^BASE_URL=/{gsub(/^"|"$/,"",$2); gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/,"",$2); print $2}' .env.production 2>/dev/null | tail -n 1)
    base_url="${BASE_URL:-${base_url:-https://soullab.life}}"
    base_url="${base_url%/}"  # Strip trailing slash

    log_info "  Target: $base_url"

    local all_passed=true
    local report=""
    add_result() { report="${report}\n  $1"; }

    # Wait for Next.js cold start (standalone server needs time)
    log_info "  Waiting for services to stabilize..."
    sleep 8

    # Helper: retry a curl check up to N times with backoff (explicit timeouts)
    retry_curl() {
        local url="$1"
        local max_attempts="${2:-3}"
        local attempt=1
        while [ $attempt -le $max_attempts ]; do
            if curl -sf --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 8 "$url" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
                return 0
            fi
            sleep 2
            attempt=$((attempt + 1))
        done
        return 1
    }

    # Test 1: Health endpoint (with retry for cold start)
    log_info "  Testing /api/health..."
    if retry_curl "${base_url}/api/health" 3; then
        log_success "  /api/health OK"
        add_result "PASS  /api/health"
    else
        log_error "  /api/health FAILED"
        add_result "FAIL  /api/health (unreachable after retries)"
        send_alert "critical" "Health endpoint failed after deployment"
        all_passed=false
    fi

    # Test 2: Version endpoint (with retry for cold start)
    log_info "  Testing /api/version..."
    if retry_curl "${base_url}/api/version" 3; then
        log_success "  /api/version OK"
        add_result "PASS  /api/version"
    else
        log_error "  /api/version FAILED"
        add_result "FAIL  /api/version (unreachable after retries)"
        send_alert "critical" "Version endpoint failed after deployment"
        all_passed=false
    fi

    # Test 3: Ready endpoint (checks dependencies)
    log_info "  Testing /api/ready..."
    local ready_response
    ready_response=$(curl -sf --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 8 "${base_url}/api/ready" 2>/dev/null || echo '{"ready":false}')
    if echo "$ready_response" | grep -q '"ready":true'; then
        log_success "  /api/ready OK"
        add_result "PASS  /api/ready"
    else
        log_warn "  /api/ready shows degraded dependencies"
        add_result "WARN  /api/ready (degraded dependencies)"
        # Build safe JSON payload for alert
        local ready_snip
        ready_snip="$(echo "$ready_response" | head -c 500)"
        local payload
        if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            payload="$(jq -n --arg response "$ready_snip" '{response:$response}')"
        else
            payload="{\"response\":\"$(echo "$ready_snip" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g')\"}"
        fi
        send_alert "warning" "Dependencies degraded after deployment" "$payload"
    fi

    # Test 4: Main page loads
    log_info "  Testing main page..."
    if curl -sf --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 10 "${base_url}/" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        log_success "  Main page OK"
        add_result "PASS  Main page"
    else
        log_warn "  Main page may be slow to respond"
        add_result "WARN  Main page (slow or unreachable)"
    fi

    # Test 5: Auth endpoints are locked (with retry for cold start)
    # Helper for status code checks with retry
    get_status_code_with_retry() {
        local url="$1"
        local method="${2:-GET}"
        local max_attempts=3
        local attempt=1
        local code
        while [ $attempt -le $max_attempts ]; do
            if [ "$method" = "POST" ]; then
                code=$(curl -sS --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 8 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST "$url" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{}' 2>/dev/null)
            else
                code=$(curl -sS --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 8 -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" "$url" 2>/dev/null)
            fi
            # If we got a real response (not warmup noise), return it
            # 000 = curl couldn't connect, 500/502/504 = gateway errors during boot
            if [ "$code" != "000" ] && [ "$code" != "500" ] && [ "$code" != "502" ] && [ "$code" != "504" ]; then
                echo "$code"
                return 0
            fi
            sleep 2
            attempt=$((attempt + 1))
        done
        echo "$code"  # Return last code even if it's 500
    }

    # Only accept HTTP→HTTPS redirects when testing localhost (prevents masking real security issues)
    local allow_redirect_as_pass=false
    if echo "$base_url" | grep -qE '^http://(localhost|127\.0\.0\.1)(:|/|$)'; then
        allow_redirect_as_pass=true
    fi

    log_info "  Testing auth lock on /api/build/status..."
    local status_code
    status_code=$(get_status_code_with_retry "${base_url}/api/build/status" "GET")
    if [ "$status_code" = "000" ]; then
        log_error "  /api/build/status unreachable (000) — check routing/DNS/caddy"
        add_result "FAIL  /api/build/status (000 - routing issue)"
        all_passed=false
    elif $allow_redirect_as_pass && { [ "$status_code" = "301" ] || [ "$status_code" = "308" ]; }; then
        # HTTP→HTTPS redirect is acceptable for localhost smoke tests only
        log_success "  /api/build/status redirects to HTTPS ($status_code) — acceptable for localhost HTTP smoke only"
        add_result "PASS  /api/build/status (redirect: $status_code, localhost only)"
    elif [ "$status_code" = "401" ] || [ "$status_code" = "403" ] || [ "$status_code" = "503" ]; then
        log_success "  /api/build/status locked ($status_code)"
        add_result "PASS  /api/build/status (locked: $status_code)"
    else
        log_error "  /api/build/status NOT LOCKED (got $status_code, expected 401/403/503)"
        add_result "FAIL  /api/build/status (got $status_code, not locked)"
        send_alert "critical" "Build status endpoint is not protected!" "{\"http_code\": \"$status_code\"}"
        all_passed=false
    fi

    log_info "  Testing auth lock on /api/build/alert..."
    status_code=$(get_status_code_with_retry "${base_url}/api/build/alert" "POST")
    if [ "$status_code" = "000" ]; then
        log_error "  /api/build/alert unreachable (000) — check routing/DNS/caddy"
        add_result "FAIL  /api/build/alert (000 - routing issue)"
        all_passed=false
    elif $allow_redirect_as_pass && { [ "$status_code" = "301" ] || [ "$status_code" = "308" ]; }; then
        # HTTP→HTTPS redirect is acceptable for localhost smoke tests only
        log_success "  /api/build/alert redirects to HTTPS ($status_code) — acceptable for localhost HTTP smoke only"
        add_result "PASS  /api/build/alert (redirect: $status_code, localhost only)"
    elif [ "$status_code" = "401" ] || [ "$status_code" = "403" ]; then
        log_success "  /api/build/alert locked ($status_code)"
        add_result "PASS  /api/build/alert (locked: $status_code)"
    elif [ "$status_code" = "503" ]; then
        # 503 to an unauthenticated probe = INTERNAL_ALERT_TOKEN unset: the route is
        # closed, but ALSO cannot deliver any alert. Not "locked" — unconfigured.
        log_warn "  /api/build/alert UNCONFIGURED (503) — closed, but deploy alerts cannot be delivered"
        add_result "WARN  /api/build/alert (503: alert path unconfigured — alerts undeliverable)"
    else
        log_error "  /api/build/alert NOT LOCKED (got $status_code, expected 401/403/503)"
        add_result "FAIL  /api/build/alert (got $status_code, not locked)"
        send_alert "critical" "Build alert endpoint is not protected!" "{\"http_code\": \"$status_code\"}"
        all_passed=false
    fi

    # ── Constitutional Verification Gate ───────────────────────────────────────
    # Runs the full constitutional verification suite inside the container.
    # Checks all five subsystems: Co-Lab, Memory, Relationships, Development, MAIA.
    # Skipped gracefully if the orchestrator is absent (first-time deploys).
    # A non-zero exit is a hard release failure.
    #
    # Gate invariant: a release is not ready because the UI looks correct —
    # it is ready when the platform proves it still honors its constitution.
    log_info "  Running constitutional verification..."
    if docker exec maia-sovereign test -f /app/scripts/constitutional-verification.sh 2>/dev/null; then
        local cv_output
        if cv_output=$(docker exec maia-sovereign sh -c \
            'DATABASE_URL="$DATABASE_URL" bash scripts/constitutional-verification.sh 2>&1'); then
            log_success "  Constitutional verification: PASSED"
            add_result "PASS  Constitutional verification (Co-Lab + Memory + Relationships + Development + MAIA)"
        else
            log_error "  Constitutional verification FAILED"
            echo "$cv_output" | grep -E "FAIL|Release gate" >&2
            add_result "FAIL  Constitutional verification — run: docker exec maia-sovereign sh -c 'DATABASE_URL=\"\$DATABASE_URL\" bash scripts/constitutional-verification.sh'"
            all_passed=false
        fi
    else
        log_warn "  constitutional-verification.sh not found in container — skipping (deploy in progress?)"
        add_result "SKIP  Constitutional verification (script not in image)"
    fi

    # Print summary report
    echo -e "\n${CYAN}═══ Smoke Test Report ═══${NC}${report}\n"

    if $all_passed; then
        log_success "All smoke tests passed!"
        send_alert "info" "Deployment successful - all smoke tests passed"
    else
        log_error "Some smoke tests failed!"
        return 1
    fi
}

# SETUP - First-time initialization
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
cmd_setup() {
    log_info "Setting up MAIA Sovereign production environment..."

    cd "$PROJECT_DIR"

    # Check if .env.production exists
    if [ -f ".env.production" ]; then
        log_warn ".env.production already exists. Skipping creation."
        log_info "To regenerate, delete it first: rm .env.production"
    else
        log_info "Creating .env.production from template..."
        cp .env.production.template .env.production

        # Generate secrets
        log_info "Generating secure secrets..."

        POSTGRES_PASS=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
        JWT_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 64)
        AUDIT_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)

        # Replace placeholders (macOS-compatible sed)
        if [[ "$OSTYPE" == "darwin"* ]]; then
            sed -i '' "s/POSTGRES_PASSWORD=.*/POSTGRES_PASSWORD=$POSTGRES_PASS/" .env.production
            sed -i '' "s/JWT_SECRET=.*/JWT_SECRET=$JWT_SECRET/" .env.production
            sed -i '' "s/MAIA_AUDIT_FINGERPRINT_SECRET=.*/MAIA_AUDIT_FINGERPRINT_SECRET=$AUDIT_SECRET/" .env.production
        else
            sed -i "s/POSTGRES_PASSWORD=.*/POSTGRES_PASSWORD=$POSTGRES_PASS/" .env.production
            sed -i "s/JWT_SECRET=.*/JWT_SECRET=$JWT_SECRET/" .env.production
            sed -i "s/MAIA_AUDIT_FINGERPRINT_SECRET=.*/MAIA_AUDIT_FINGERPRINT_SECRET=$AUDIT_SECRET/" .env.production
        fi

        log_success "Secrets generated and saved to .env.production"

        echo ""
        log_warn "IMPORTANT: Edit .env.production to set:"
        echo "  - BASE_URL (your domain)"
        echo "  - ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
        echo "  - ELEVENLABS_API_KEY (if using voice)"
        echo ""
    fi

    # Update DATABASE_URL with the password
    log_info "Updating DATABASE_URL..."
    POSTGRES_PASS=$(grep "^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=" .env.production | cut -d'=' -f2)
    if [[ "$OSTYPE" == "darwin"* ]]; then
        sed -i '' "s|DATABASE_URL=.*|DATABASE_URL=postgresql://soullab:${POSTGRES_PASS}@postgres:5432/maia_consciousness|" .env.production
    else
        sed -i "s|DATABASE_URL=.*|DATABASE_URL=postgresql://soullab:${POSTGRES_PASS}@postgres:5432/maia_consciousness|" .env.production
    fi

    log_success "Setup complete! Next steps:"
    echo "  1. Edit .env.production with your domain and API keys"
    echo "  2. Run: ./scripts/deploy-production.sh deploy"
}

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# DEPLOY - Build and start the stack
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
cmd_deploy() {
    local ref="${1:-}"
    # The lock record names the ASSERTED target (the SHA on the command line),
    # never the shared checkout's HEAD — see scripts/deploy-lock.sh.
    acquire_deploy_lock "deploy-production.sh deploy" "$ref"
    log_info "Deploying MAIA Sovereign..."

    cd "$PROJECT_DIR"

    # Name a commit and snapshot it into an isolated build context BEFORE any
    # build work. Refuses when no SHA is named (unless DEPLOY_ALLOW_HEAD=1). This
    # is the structural guarantee that the full deploy builds an explicitly named
    # immutable commit, never whichever branch happens to be checked out in the
    # shared repo. Sets MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT + GIT_COMMIT.
    deploy_ctx_assert_and_materialize "$ref" || exit 1
    deploy_ctx_assert_descends_from_running "deploy-production.sh deploy" || exit 1

    # Verify .env.production exists
    if [ ! -f ".env.production" ]; then
        log_error ".env.production not found. Run: ./scripts/deploy-production.sh setup"

    fi

    if grep -q "REPLACE_ME" .env.production; then
        log_error "Please replace all REPLACE_ME values in .env.production"
        exit 1
    fi

    # Dependency security audit — target-declared manager, fail closed at moderate+.
    run_dependency_security_audit || exit 1

    # Build and start
    log_info "Building Docker images..."
    # GIT_COMMIT was exported from the asserted SHA by materialize above — do NOT
    # re-resolve it from HEAD here (that would re-couple us to the shared checkout).
    # APP_VERSION is read from the SNAPSHOT so it matches the deployed commit.
    export APP_VERSION="$(node -p "require('$MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT/package.json').version" 2>/dev/null || echo '1.0.0')"
    export BUILD_DATE="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
    log_info "Deploying commit: $GIT_COMMIT (v$APP_VERSION)"

    # Disk preflight — refuse BEFORE the storage-expanding build (a full-disk
    # build dies at metadata write after minutes and can exit 0 through ssh).
    "$SCRIPT_DIR/pre-deploy-gate.sh" disk

    # Build image first (never rebuild while down!) — from the immutable snapshot
    # (compose reads MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT for every build `context:`).
    # Build + swap use the SNAPSHOT's compose file (deploy_ctx_compose) — the
    # deployment structure is the authorized commit's (2026-09-03 provenance repair).
    # :prod guard: the build moves :prod; restore it if we stop before the swap.
    prod_tag_guard_arm "$GIT_COMMIT"
    deploy_ctx_compose build \
        --build-arg GIT_COMMIT="$GIT_COMMIT" \
        --build-arg APP_VERSION="$APP_VERSION" \
        --build-arg BUILD_DATE="$BUILD_DATE"

    # PRE-swap: the built image must carry the asserted stamp; abort before any swap.
    deploy_ctx_verify_image "$GIT_COMMIT" "$MAIA_IMAGE_REPO:prod" || exit 1

    # REVIEW-CUSTODY + DS-03: the exact pending relation must carry an
    # admitted review, exact old-reader compatibility, and failure-prefix safety.
    review_migration_custody_or_abort "Deployment"

    # STEP 3: migrate while the reviewed old reader is still live. The helper
    # re-derives the pending set and re-witnesses the old reader immediately
    # before invoking the runner. Failure exits here, before tags or candidate swap.
    run_migrations_or_abort "Deployment"

    # Only a successful pre-swap migration may advance rollback roles or the reader.
    # From here the candidate is the legitimate :prod.
    prod_tag_guard_disarm
    tag_images_for_rollback "$GIT_COMMIT"

    log_info "Starting containers after successful migrations..."
    deploy_ctx_compose up -d

    log_info "Waiting for services to be healthy..."
    sleep 10

    # Post-swap: assert the running container is the commit we authorized.
    if ! deploy_ctx_verify_running "$GIT_COMMIT"; then
        log_error "Post-swap provenance verification FAILED — the running container does not report the"
        log_error "authorized immutable commit $GIT_COMMIT. Migrations already succeeded pre-swap."
        log_error "The reviewed old reader was compatible with the resulting schema; restore the"
        log_error "previous reader image if the candidate cannot be made live (rollback stops the"
        log_error "candidate and refuses to swap if scripts/rollback-guards/ finds rows the old reader"
        log_error "cannot read; it prints the repair to run first):"
        log_error "  ./scripts/deploy-production.sh rollback"
        exit 1
    fi

    log_success "Deployment complete!"
    echo ""
    cmd_status

    # Run smoke tests and send alerts
    echo ""
    run_smoke_tests || log_warn "Some post-deploy checks failed"
}

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# UPDATE - Pull latest and redeploy
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
cmd_update() {
    # No commit is named yet — `update` names the tip it pulls, below. The
    # record is re-written with that SHA the moment the pull completes.
    acquire_deploy_lock "deploy-production.sh update" "pending (tip pulled by git pull; recorded once the pull completes)"
    log_info "Updating MAIA Sovereign..."

    cd "$PROJECT_DIR"

    log_info "Pulling latest code..."
    git pull

    # Capture the pulled tip as an explicit, immutable SHA the instant the pull
    # completes, then build a SNAPSHOT of it. `update` legitimately means "build
    # the commit I just pulled" — but it must name that commit and freeze it, so
    # a concurrent checkout in the shared repo can't swap the build out from under
    # us. Sets MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT + GIT_COMMIT.
    local pulled_sha
    pulled_sha="$(git -C "$PROJECT_DIR" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)"
    deploy_lock_record_target "$pulled_sha"
    deploy_ctx_assert_and_materialize "$pulled_sha" || exit 1
    deploy_ctx_assert_descends_from_running "deploy-production.sh update" || exit 1

    log_info "Rebuilding and redeploying..."

    # Dependency security audit — target-declared manager, fail closed at moderate+.
    run_dependency_security_audit || exit 1

    # GIT_COMMIT was exported from the pulled SHA by materialize above; APP_VERSION
    # is read from the SNAPSHOT so it matches the deployed commit.
    export APP_VERSION="$(node -p "require('$MAIA_BUILD_CONTEXT/package.json').version" 2>/dev/null || echo '1.0.0')"
    export BUILD_DATE="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
    log_info "Deploying commit: $GIT_COMMIT (v$APP_VERSION)"

    # Disk preflight — refuse BEFORE the storage-expanding build (a full-disk
    # build dies at metadata write after minutes and can exit 0 through ssh).
    "$SCRIPT_DIR/pre-deploy-gate.sh" disk

    # Build + swap from the immutable snapshot — code AND compose structure
    # (deploy_ctx_compose; 2026-09-03 provenance repair).
    # :prod guard: the build moves :prod; restore it if we stop before the swap.
    prod_tag_guard_arm "$GIT_COMMIT"
    deploy_ctx_compose build \
        --build-arg GIT_COMMIT="$GIT_COMMIT" \
        --build-arg APP_VERSION="$APP_VERSION" \
        --build-arg BUILD_DATE="$BUILD_DATE"

    # PRE-swap: the built image must carry the asserted stamp; abort before any swap.
    deploy_ctx_verify_image "$GIT_COMMIT" "$MAIA_IMAGE_REPO:prod" || exit 1

    # REVIEW-CUSTODY + DS-03: same exact relation gate on update.
    review_migration_custody_or_abort "Update"

    # STEP 3: no candidate reader is swapped until the reviewed schema transition
    # succeeds while the exact old reader remains live.
    run_migrations_or_abort "Update"

    # Rollback roles advance only after the pre-swap schema transition succeeds.
    # From here the candidate is the legitimate :prod.
    prod_tag_guard_disarm
    tag_images_for_rollback "$GIT_COMMIT"

    deploy_ctx_compose up -d

    # Post-swap: assert the running container is the commit we authorized.
    sleep 10
    if ! deploy_ctx_verify_running "$GIT_COMMIT"; then
        log_error "Post-swap provenance verification FAILED — the running container does not report the"
        log_error "authorized immutable commit $GIT_COMMIT. Migrations already succeeded pre-swap."
        log_error "The reviewed old reader was compatible with the resulting schema; restore the"
        log_error "previous reader image if the candidate cannot be made live (rollback stops the"
        log_error "candidate and refuses to swap if scripts/rollback-guards/ finds rows the old reader"
        log_error "cannot read; it prints the repair to run first):"
        log_error "  ./scripts/deploy-production.sh rollback"
        exit 1
    fi

    log_success "Update complete!"
    cmd_status

    # Run smoke tests and send alerts
    echo ""
    run_smoke_tests || log_warn "Some post-deploy checks failed"
}

# MIGRATE - Run database migrations only
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
cmd_migrate() {
    local ref="${1:-}"
    if [ -z "$ref" ]; then
        log_error "Migration-only production acts require an explicit target SHA."
        log_error "Usage: ./scripts/deploy-production.sh migrate <SHA>"
        exit 1
    fi

    acquire_deploy_lock "deploy-production.sh migrate" "$ref"
    log_info "Running database migrations for exact target: $ref"

    cd "$PROJECT_DIR"

    # ⭐ Migration-only is not a mutable-checkout escape hatch. Materialize the
    # exact reviewed target so discovery, custody and execution all read the same
    # immutable bytes as deploy/update.
    deploy_ctx_assert_and_materialize "$ref" || exit 1
    deploy_ctx_assert_descends_from_running "deploy-production.sh migrate" || exit 1

    # Migration-only production acts are governed by the same bound review.
    review_migration_custody_or_abort "Migration-only run"

    # Re-witness the pending set + old reader at the last possible point and run
    # migrations from the immutable target context. No candidate reader is swapped.
    run_migrations_or_abort "Migration-only run"

    log_success "Migrations complete!"
}

cmd_restore() {
    if [ -z "$1" ]; then
        log_error "Usage: ./deploy-production.sh restore <backup_file.sql>"
        exit 1
    fi

    BACKUP_FILE="$1"

    if [ ! -f "$BACKUP_FILE" ]; then
        log_error "Backup file not found: $BACKUP_FILE"
        exit 1

    log_warn "This will REPLACE all data in the database!"

        psql -U soullab maia_consciousness < "$BACKUP_FILE"

    log_success "Database restored!"
}

# ROLLBACK - Instant rollback to previous deployment
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Two-command rollback: swap image tags, restart container
# No rebuild required - just swap and go

# Commit an image was built from: the git.commit label, else its baked GIT_COMMIT.
rollback_image_commit() {
    local image="$1" sha
    sha="$(docker image inspect "$image" --format '{{index .Config.Labels "git.commit"}}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ -z "$sha" ] || [ "$sha" = "<no value>" ]; then
        sha="$(docker image inspect "$image" --format '{{range .Config.Env}}{{println .}}{{end}}' 2>/dev/null \
            | sed -n 's/^GIT_COMMIT=//p' | head -1)"
    fi
    echo "${sha:-unknown}"
}

# Guard file for a commit: scripts/rollback-guards/<full sha>.sql, matched by prefix
# (images carry short SHAs). Repair files (*.repair.sql) are never guards.
rollback_guard_for() {
    local sha="$1" f stem
    [ "${#sha}" -ge 7 ] || return 0
    case "$sha" in *[!0-9a-f]*) return 0 ;; esac
    for f in "$SCRIPT_DIR"/rollback-guards/*.sql; do
        [ -e "$f" ] || continue
        case "$f" in *.repair.sql) continue ;; esac
        stem="$(basename "$f" .sql)"
        case "$stem" in "$sha"*) echo "$f"; return 0 ;; esac
    done
}

# True when a commit value is a hex SHA long enough to match a guard file.
rollback_commit_resolvable() {
    [ "${#1}" -ge 7 ] || return 1
    case "$1" in *[!0-9a-f]*) return 1 ;; esac
}

# True when at least one guard (not a repair file) is present.
rollback_guards_exist() {
    local f
    for f in "$SCRIPT_DIR"/rollback-guards/*.sql; do
        [ -e "$f" ] || continue
        case "$f" in *.repair.sql) continue ;; esac
        return 0
    done
    return 1
}

# Runs a guard's read-only count; prints the number of rows the old reader would refuse.
rollback_guard_count() {
    local out
    out="$(docker exec -i maia-postgres psql -U soullab -d maia_consciousness -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -At < "$1")" || return 1
    out="$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | tail -1 | tr -d '[:space:]')"
    case "$out" in ''|*[!0-9]*) return 1 ;; esac
    echo "$out"
}

# Check if previous image exists
    if ! docker image inspect maia-sovereign:previous >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        log_error "No previous image found. Cannot rollback."
        log_info "Previous images are created during deploy. Run deploy at least twice."
        exit 1
    fi

    # Get current and previous commit SHAs (label first, then the GIT_COMMIT baked into the image)
    CURRENT_SHA=$(rollback_image_commit maia-sovereign:current)
    PREVIOUS_SHA=$(rollback_image_commit maia-sovereign:previous)

    log_info "Current deployment: $CURRENT_SHA"
    log_info "Rolling back to: $PREVIOUS_SHA"

    # Data guard: a newer schema may have admitted rows the previous reader cannot
    # read. If a guard exists for the commit being restored, stop the current reader
    # (so it writes no more such rows) and refuse to swap while any remain.
    # A guard covers only the commit it is named for. Rolling back to any other
    # commit runs no data check: that rollback needs its own review and guard.
    local guard_file
    guard_file="$(rollback_guard_for "$PREVIOUS_SHA")"
    # Fail closed: if guards exist but the restored image's commit cannot be resolved,
    # no guard can be matched, so refuse rather than skip the check silently.
    if [ -z "$guard_file" ] && ! rollback_commit_resolvable "$PREVIOUS_SHA" \
       && rollback_guards_exist && [ "${ROLLBACK_UNKNOWN_COMMIT_ACK:-}" != "1" ]; then
        log_error "Rollback refused: cannot resolve the commit of maia-sovereign:previous ('$PREVIOUS_SHA'),"
        log_error "so no rollback data guard in scripts/rollback-guards/ can be matched to it."
        log_error "Confirm by hand that the previous reader can read current data, then re-run with"
        log_error "  ROLLBACK_UNKNOWN_COMMIT_ACK=1 ./scripts/deploy-production.sh rollback"
        exit 1
    fi
    if [ -n "$guard_file" ]; then
        log_info "Rollback data guard for $PREVIOUS_SHA: $guard_file"
        log_info "Stopping the current reader before checking stored data..."
        docker stop maia-sovereign >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
        if [ "$(docker inspect maia-sovereign --format '{{.State.Running}}' 2>/dev/null || echo false)" = "true" ]; then
            log_error "Rollback refused: maia-sovereign is still running after docker stop, so it could"
            log_error "still write rows the previous reader cannot read. No tag has moved."
            exit 1
        fi
        local failing
        if ! failing="$(rollback_guard_count "$guard_file")"; then
            log_error "Rollback data guard could not run. Refusing to swap; the current reader is stopped."
            log_error "To keep the current release instead of rolling back, start it again (no tag has moved):"
            log_error "  docker start maia-sovereign"
            exit 1
        fi
        if [ "$failing" != "0" ]; then
            log_error "Rollback refused: $failing stored row(s) would break the reader at $PREVIOUS_SHA."
            log_error "The current reader is stopped. Repair the rows, then run rollback again:"
            log_error "  docker exec -i maia-postgres psql -U soullab -d maia_consciousness -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 < ${guard_file%.sql}.repair.sql"
            log_error "  ./scripts/deploy-production.sh rollback"
            log_error "Or, to keep the current release instead (no tag has moved):"
            log_error "  docker start maia-sovereign"
            exit 1
        fi
        log_success "Rollback data guard: 0 rows the previous reader would refuse."
    else
        log_info "No rollback data guard is named for $PREVIOUS_SHA; no stored-data check runs."
    fi

    # Resolve image identities before moving any role tags.
    local current_id previous_id
    current_id="$(docker image inspect maia-sovereign:current --format '{{.Id}}')"
    previous_id="$(docker image inspect maia-sovereign:previous --format '{{.Id}}')"
    if [ -z "$current_id" ] || [ -z "$previous_id" ]; then
        log_error "Rollback image identity is incomplete; refusing to move role tags."
        exit 1
    fi

    # Compose launches maia-sovereign:prod, not :current. Therefore rollback must
    # move the previous image onto BOTH role tags before recreating the reader.
    log_info "Swapping image tags..."
    docker tag maia-sovereign:current maia-sovereign:broken
    docker tag maia-sovereign:previous maia-sovereign:current
    docker tag maia-sovereign:previous maia-sovereign:prod

    # Restart only the application reader. A reader rollback must not restart
    # Postgres or any other dependency.
    log_info "Restarting MAIA with previous image..."
    docker compose -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" up -d --force-recreate --no-deps maia

    # Wait for health
    log_info "Waiting for service to be healthy..."
    sleep 10

    # Verify both health and that Compose actually launched the previous image.
    local running_id running_git
    running_id="$(docker inspect maia-sovereign --format '{{.Image}}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
    running_git="$(docker exec maia-sovereign printenv GIT_COMMIT 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if docker compose -f "$COMPOSE_FILE" ps | grep -q "healthy" \
       && [ "$running_id" = "$previous_id" ]; then
        if [ -n "$guard_file" ]; then
            local after
            after="$(rollback_guard_count "$guard_file" || echo "error")"
            if [ "$after" != "0" ]; then
                log_error "Rollback swapped, but the data guard now reports: $after. Investigate before serving traffic."
                exit 1
            fi
        fi
        log_success "Rollback complete! Now running: ${running_git:-$PREVIOUS_SHA}"

        # Move the former reader to :previous so an explicit roll-forward remains possible.
        docker tag maia-sovereign:broken maia-sovereign:previous

        send_alert "warning" "Rollback executed" "{\"from\": \"$CURRENT_SHA\", \"to\": \"${running_git:-$PREVIOUS_SHA}\"}"
    else
        log_error "Rollback verification FAILED."
        log_error "Expected running image: $previous_id"
        log_error "Observed running image: ${running_id:-<missing>}"
        cmd_status
        exit 1
    fi
}

cmd_safe_mode() {
    local mode="${1:-status}"
    cd "$PROJECT_DIR"

    case "$mode" in
        on|enable|1)
            log_info "Enabling safe mode..."

            # Set SAFE_MODE=1 in .env.production if not already set
